title.zh: 卷361 列傳一百四十八 刘清 傅鼐 严如熤子：正基
title.en: Volume 361 Biographies 148: Liu Qing, Fu Nai, Yan Ruyi Son: Zheng Ji
title.raw: 卷361 列傳一百四十八 刘清 傅鼐 严如熤子：正基

sentences.zh: 列傳一百四十八

translations.literal: Biographies 148
translations.idiomatic: Biography 148

sentences.zh: 劉清傅鼐嚴如熤子正基

translations.literal: Liu Qing, Fu Nai, Yan Ruyi; son: Zheng Ji
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing, Fu Nai, and Yan Ruyi; Yan's son Zheng Ji

sentences.zh: 劉清，字天一，貴州廣順人。

translations.literal: Liu Qing, courtesy name Tianyi, was a native of Guangshun in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing, styled Tianyi, came from Guangshun in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 由拔貢議敘，授四川冕寧縣丞，擢南充知縣，政聲為一省之冠。

translations.literal: Having risen through the tribute-student route and received an appointment by memorial, he was posted as assistant magistrate of Mianning County in Sichuan, then promoted to magistrate of Nanchong; his reputation for good government ranked first in the province.
translations.idiomatic: After qualifying as a tribute student and receiving an appointment through memorial review, he served as assistant magistrate of Mianning in Sichuan, then rose to magistrate of Nanchong, where his reputation for governance stood at the top of the province.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，教匪起，清得民心，募鄉勇五百人擊賊，人樂為用。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Jiaqing reign, when the teaching rebels rose, Qing won the hearts of the people, raised five hundred local militiamen to strike the bandits, and men were glad to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 1, when sectarian rebels broke out, Qing had the people's trust; he recruited five hundred village braves to fight the rebels, and men gladly served under him.

sentences.zh: 賊自為民時知其名，遇輒避之。

translations.literal: The bandits had known his name when they were still ordinary people, and whenever they met him they would give way.
translations.idiomatic: Even when they had been common folk, the rebels knew his name; whenever they encountered him they steered clear.

sentences.zh: 繼從總督英善剿達州匪徐天德，數捷，率鄉勇羅思舉赴賊營諭降羅其清，未得要領；

translations.literal: He then followed Governor Yingshan in suppressing the Dazhou rebel Xu Tiande, won repeated victories, and led the militiaman Luo Siju to the rebel camp to persuade Luo Qiqi to surrender, but without securing a clear agreement;
translations.idiomatic: He next served under Governor Yingshan against the Dazhou rebel Xu Tiande, won several victories, and took the militia leader Luo Siju to the rebel camp to urge Luo Qiqi to surrender, but gained no firm pledge;

sentences.zh: 而徐天德與王三槐、冷天祿合陷東鄉，二年春，始復之，遂署東鄉。

translations.literal: Xu Tiande meanwhile joined Wang Sanhuai and Leng Tianlu in seizing Dongxiang; in the spring of the second year it was recovered, and Qing was put in charge of Dongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Xu Tiande, Wang Sanhuai, and Leng Tianlu together overran Dongxiang; in spring of the second year the place was retaken, and Qing was appointed to administer it.

sentences.zh: 進克清谿場，擒賊黨王學禮，天德之舅也，言天德與王三槐皆有歸順意。

translations.literal: Advancing, he took Qingxi Field, captured the rebel partisan Wang Xueli—Xu Tiande's maternal uncle—who said that Xu and Wang Sanhuai both wished to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and captured Qingxi Field, seizing the partisan Wang Xueli, Xu Tiande's uncle by marriage, who reported that Xu and Wang Sanhuai were both inclined to surrender.

sentences.zh: 總督宜綿令清往招三槐，遍歷諸賊壘，迎送奉酒食甚謹，宣示招撫，皆聽命，夜宿其帳中。

translations.literal: Governor Yimian ordered Qing to go and win over Sanhuai; he went through every rebel stockade, was received with great courtesy and offered food and drink, proclaimed the policy of pacification, and all obeyed; he even spent the night in their tents.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yimian sent Qing to recruit Sanhuai; he visited every rebel stronghold, was escorted in with wine and food, announced the offer of amnesty, and all assented; he even lodged overnight in their camps.

sentences.zh: 三槐隨至大營，約期率所部出降，然實藉覘虛實，非真意。

translations.literal: Sanhuai followed him to headquarters and agreed on a date to lead his followers out in surrender, but in fact he was using the chance to spy on strength and weakness, not acting in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Sanhuai came to the main camp and fixed a day to bring his men out in surrender, but he was really reconnoitering the army's condition, not sincere.

sentences.zh: 屆期，三槐詭稱於雙廟投降，伏匪為掩襲計，官軍預設備，擊敗之。

translations.literal: When the day came, Sanhuai falsely claimed he would surrender at Shuangmiao Temple while hiding rebels for a surprise attack; the government troops were prepared in advance and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day Sanhuai pretended he would surrender at Shuangmiao Temple while rebels lay in ambush for a surprise strike; the government forces were ready and beat them off.

sentences.zh: 時羅其清、冉文儔並聚方山坪，清偕總兵百祥奪多福山賊壘，會諸路兵攻方山坪，克之。

translations.literal: At that time Luo Qiqi and Ran Wenchou were both gathered at Fangshanping; Qing with Brigadier Bai Xiang seized the rebel stronghold on Duofu Mountain, joined troops from every route in attacking Fangshanping, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Qiqi and Ran Wenchou were then massed at Fangshanping; Qing with Brigadier Bai Xiang stormed the Duofu Mountain stockade, combined with columns from every direction against Fangshanping, and captured it.

sentences.zh: 賊竄通江、巴州，與徐天德、王三槐合，清所部鄉勇增至千餘人，桂涵、李子青等皆驍勇善戰，偕諸軍擊賊，疊有殲獲，羅、冉二匪漸蹙。

translations.literal: The rebels fled into Tongjiang and Bazhou and joined Xu Tiande and Wang Sanhuai; Qing's militia grew to more than a thousand, and Gui Han, Li Ziqing, and others were all fierce fighters; fighting alongside the regular armies they won repeated kills and captures, and the Luo and Ran bands were gradually cornered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels slipped into Tongjiang and Bazhou and united with Xu Tiande and Wang Sanhuai; Qing's militia swelled past a thousand, with Gui Han, Li Ziqing, and others all seasoned fighters; fighting with the regular forces they piled up kills and captures until the Luo and Ran bands were nearly spent.

sentences.zh: 三年，署廣元縣事。

translations.literal: In the third year he was put in charge of Guangyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was assigned to administer Guangyuan County.

sentences.zh: 總督勒保攻王三槐於安樂坪，未下，復令清往招撫。

translations.literal: Governor Lebao attacked Wang Sanhuai at Anleping without success and again ordered Qing to go and offer pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Lebao besieged Wang Sanhuai at Anleping without success and again sent Qing to negotiate surrender.

sentences.zh: 三槐恃前此出入大營無忌，留隨人劉星渠等為質，三槐遂詣軍門，勒保奏報大捷，俘三槐至京。

translations.literal: Sanhuai, relying on his earlier freedom to enter and leave the main camp, left Liu Xingqu and others of his party as hostages, then came to the army gate; Lebao memorialized a great victory and sent Sanhuai captive to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Sanhuai, trusting his earlier liberty in the main camp, left Liu Xingqu and others as hostages, then presented himself at headquarters; Lebao reported a great victory and sent Sanhuai to the capital as a prisoner.

sentences.zh: 廷訊時，言：「官逼民反。」

translations.literal: At his interrogation in court he said: "Officials drove the people to rebel."
translations.idiomatic: At his examination at court he said, "The officials drove the people to rebel."

sentences.zh: 仁宗詰之曰：「四川一省官皆不善耶？」

translations.literal: The Emperor Renzong questioned him: "Are all the officials of Sichuan province bad?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong pressed him: "Are every one of Sichuan's officials wicked?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「惟有劉青天一人。」

translations.literal: He answered: "There is only one—Liu the Blue Sky."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "There is only one—Liu the Blue Sky."

sentences.zh: 劉青天者，川民以呼清也。

translations.literal: "Liu the Blue Sky" was what the people of Sichuan called Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu the Blue Sky was the name the people of Sichuan gave Qing.

sentences.zh: 帝深嘉之，特諭曰：「朕聞劉清官聲甚好，每率眾禦敵，賊以其廉吏，往往退避引去。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly praised this and issued a special edict: "We have heard that Liu Qing's official reputation is excellent; he always leads his men against the enemy, and the bandits, because he is an upright official, often withdraw and slip away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply pleased and issued a special instruction: "We hear Liu Qing's reputation as an official is excellent; he always leads his men against the enemy, and the rebels, seeing an honest magistrate, often draw off and leave.

sentences.zh: 如果始終奮勇，民情愛戴，著勒保據實保奏。」

translations.literal: If he continues brave to the end and the people love him, order Lebao to recommend him on the facts."
translations.idiomatic: If he remains valiant throughout and the people hold him dear, have Lebao report him faithfully for reward."

sentences.zh: 尋以清治績戰功奏上，晉秩同知直隸州，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Qing's record of civil achievement and military merit was submitted; he was promoted in rank to subprefect of Zhili Prefecture and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after, Qing's civil and military record was submitted; he was advanced to subprefect of Zhili Prefecture and given the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 於是劉青天之名聞天下。

translations.literal: Thus the name Liu the Blue Sky was known throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the name Liu the Blue Sky was known across the empire.

sentences.zh: 四年，補忠州，加知府銜。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed to Zhongzhou, with the rank of prefect added.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was posted to Zhongzhou with an acting prefect's rank.

sentences.zh: 參贊額勒登保破冉天元、張子聰於竹峪關，令清於通江、巴州招撫餘匪。

translations.literal: Assistant [Grand Minister] Eledengbao defeated Ran Tianyuan and Zhang Zicong at Zhuyu Pass and ordered Qing to pacify the remaining rebels in Tongjiang and Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant [Grand Minister] Eledengbao broke Ran Tianyuan and Zhang Zicong at Zhuyu Pass and ordered Qing to win over remnant rebels in Tongjiang and Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 自王三槐被誘，諸賊首皆疑憚不敢出；

translations.literal: After Wang Sanhuai was lured in, every rebel chieftain was wary and dared not come out;
translations.idiomatic: Once Wang Sanhuai had been tricked into surrender, the rebel chiefs all hung back in fear;

sentences.zh: 然感清無他，不忍加害，每至賊營，必留宿盡禮，其脅從者先後投出二萬餘人，遣散歸農，以功加道銜。

translations.literal: yet moved by Qing's sincerity they could not bear to harm him; whenever he reached a rebel camp they always lodged him with full courtesy; more than twenty thousand coerced followers came out in succession, were sent home to farm, and for this merit he was given circuit rank.
translations.idiomatic: yet trusting Qing meant them no harm, they would not hurt him; whenever he entered a rebel camp they entertained him overnight; more than twenty thousand pressed followers surrendered in turn and were sent back to the fields, and for this he received circuit rank.

sentences.zh: 命隨副都御史廣興駐達州治軍餉，擢建昌道。

translations.literal: He was ordered to accompany Vice Censor-in-Chief Guang Xing stationed at Dazhou to manage army supplies and was promoted to Jianchang Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to accompany Vice Censor Guang Xing at Dazhou to handle military provisions and was raised to intendant of Jianchang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 五年，冉天元等合諸路賊渡嘉陵江，總督魁倫退守鹽亭鳳凰山，令清集民團守潼河，上下三百餘裡，多淺灘，盡撤防兵；

translations.literal: In the fifth year Ran Tianyuan and others combined bands from every route, crossed the Jialing River; Governor Kuilun fell back to defend Fenghuang Mountain at Yanting and ordered Qing to gather civilian militia to guard the Tong River for more than three hundred li up and down—mostly shallow fords—and withdrew all garrison troops;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Ran Tianyuan united columns from every direction and crossed the Jialing; Governor Kuilun retreated to Phoenix Mountain at Yanting and told Qing to rally militia along three hundred-odd li of the Tong River, mostly shallow fords, while pulling back all regular defenders;

sentences.zh: 清爭之，不可。

translations.literal: Qing argued against it, but to no avail.
translations.idiomatic: Qing protested, but in vain.

sentences.zh: 賊果於太和鎮上游王家嘴偷渡，委罪於清，奪職，命以知縣用，留營效力。

translations.literal: The rebels did ford upstream at Wangjia Mouth above Taihe Town; blame was laid on Qing, his post was stripped, he was ordered to serve as magistrate, and kept at camp to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels forded upstream at Wangjia Mouth above Taihe Town; Qing was blamed, dismissed, ordered to serve as a magistrate, and kept in camp to atone.

sentences.zh: 既而德楞泰破賊，天元伏誅，諸路竄賊旁皇通、巴之間，勒保以清去歲招降成效，責籌安撫。

translations.literal: Later Delingtai broke the rebels, Tianyuan was executed, and scattered bands from every route wandered between Tong and Ba; Lebao, because Qing's pacification the year before had borne fruit, charged him with planning resettlement.
translations.idiomatic: Delingtai then crushed the rebels, Tianyuan was put to death, and fugitive bands roamed between Tong and Ba; Lebao, seeing last year's pacification work, put Qing in charge of resettlement.

sentences.zh: 時川匪父子兄弟一家中不盡習教為賊，而奔竄往來，過鄉里輒歸視。

translations.literal: At that time in Sichuan not every man in a rebel household had joined the sects, yet they ran back and forth in flight and, passing their home villages, would return to look in.
translations.idiomatic: In Sichuan not every son or brother in a rebel family had taken up arms, yet they shuttled in flight and, when they passed their villages, would slip home for a visit.

sentences.zh: 清屯要隘，且剿且撫，遣人存問賊首家屬有歸誠之意者，潛令圖之，展轉相引，賊遂瓦解。

translations.literal: Qing garrisoned strategic passes, fighting while also offering amnesty, sent men to inquire after rebel families who showed willingness to submit, secretly had them win others over, and by degrees the rebels fell apart.
translations.idiomatic: Qing held key passes, striking while also offering terms, sent agents to families showing good faith, quietly had them draw others in, and the rebels gradually dissolved.

sentences.zh: 藍號鮮大川，巴州人，號為狡悍。

translations.literal: Xian Dachuan of the Blue Banner, a man of Bazhou, was known as cunning and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Xian Dachuan of the Blue Banner, from Bazhou, was famed as crafty and fierce.

sentences.zh: 其族人文炳、路保及黨楊似山，清皆厚卹其家，感恩原效死，乃使文炳勸大川降，不可，且與似山謀殺文炳。

translations.literal: His clansmen Wen Bing and Lu Bao and partisan Yang Sishan—Qing had all treated their families generously; grateful, they were willing to die for him; he had Wen Bing urge Dachuan to surrender, but Dachuan refused and even plotted with Sishan to kill Wen Bing.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsmen Wen Bing and Lu Bao and follower Yang Sishan—Qing had richly provided for their households; grateful, they offered their lives; he sent Wen Bing to persuade Dachuan to surrender, but Dachuan refused and even plotted with Sishan to kill Wen Bing.

sentences.zh: 似山乘間殺大川，與文炳、路保同降。

translations.literal: Sishan seized an opening to kill Dachuan and surrendered together with Wen Bing and Lu Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Sishan seized a moment to kill Dachuan and came over with Wen Bing and Lu Bao.

sentences.zh: 巴州匪遂滅。

translations.literal: The rebels of Bazhou were thus extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The Bazhou rebels were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 六年，以功復原官，仍授建昌道。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, for merit he was restored to his former office and again appointed Jianchang intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year his former rank was restored for merit and he was again made intendant of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 七年春，破賊於南江五方坪，擒賊首李彬及辛文等，加按察使銜，尋授四川按察使。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year he defeated rebels at Wufangping in Nanjiang, captured the chiefs Li Bin and Xin Wen and others, was given surveillance-commissioner rank, and soon appointed Sichuan provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the seventh year he routed rebels at Wufangping in Nanjiang, took chiefs Li Bin and Xin Wen, received surveillance-commissioner rank, and was soon made Sichuan provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 敗藍號齊國典餘匪於兩河口，追擒其黨葛成勝。

translations.literal: He defeated remnant bandits of the Blue Banner leader Qi Guodian at Lianghekou and pursued and captured his follower Ge Chengsheng.
translations.idiomatic: He beat Qi Guodian's Blue Banner remnants at Lianghekou and ran down Ge Chengsheng.

sentences.zh: 諸匪以次平，大功告蕆，下部議敘。

translations.literal: The rebels were pacified in turn, the great task was declared complete, and the ministry was asked to record rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The bands were subdued one after another, the great campaign was declared finished, and memorials went to the ministry for rewards.

sentences.zh: 清在軍七年，先後招降三萬餘人。

translations.literal: Qing had been in the army seven years and in all had induced more than thirty thousand to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Over seven years in the field Qing had persuaded more than thirty thousand to surrender.

sentences.zh: 有業者歸鄉里，無業及有業原從者為鄉勇，後立戰功者​​三十餘人。

translations.literal: Those with livelihoods returned to their villages; those without, and those with livelihoods who had originally followed him, became militia; more than thirty of them later won military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Those with trades went home; those without, and those who had followed him despite having trades, became militia; more than thirty later distinguished themselves in battle.

sentences.zh: 其中苟崇勳、苟文耀、李彬、辛文、李世玉、趙文相，皆賊魁也。

translations.literal: Among them Gou Chongxun, Gou Wenyao, Li Bin, Xin Wen, Li Shiyu, and Zhao Wenxiang had all been rebel chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Among them Gou Chongxun, Gou Wenyao, Li Bin, Xin Wen, Li Shiyu, and Zhao Wenxiang had all been rebel leaders.

sentences.zh: 崇勳即苟文通，已奏報殲斃而改名。

translations.literal: Chongxun was in fact Gou Wentong, who had been reported killed in battle and had changed his name.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxun was Gou Wentong, already reported killed in dispatches and living under a new name.

sentences.zh: 及軍事竣，當遣，清以諸人田廬焚盪，驟散將復為賊，臨行重犒之。

translations.literal: When the campaign ended and they were to be dismissed, Qing feared that with their fields and houses burned, a sudden dispersal would make them rebels again, and on leaving he gave them heavy rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When the war ended and they were to be released, Qing feared that with homesteads in ashes a sudden breakup would turn them bandits again, and on parting he rewarded them lavishly.

sentences.zh: 自向富室巨商貸金，人感其誠，多響應。

translations.literal: He himself borrowed money from wealthy families and great merchants; moved by his sincerity, many responded.
translations.idiomatic: He borrowed from rich households and great merchants on his own credit; many answered out of respect for his honesty.

sentences.zh: 事畢，積逋負至十萬。

translations.literal: When all was done, his debts had piled up to a hundred thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: When it was over he owed a hundred thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 八年，陝西餘匪自南山竄出棧道，清馳扼廣元，遣卒招撫被戕，詔斥輕信縱賊，以前功免罪，命理糧餉及搜捕餘匪、裁撤鄉勇。

translations.literal: In the eighth year remnant rebels from Shaanxi slipped out of the Southern Mountains along the plank roads; Qing rushed to hold Guangyuan, sent men to offer pacification and they were killed; an edict rebuked him for credulity and letting rebels go, but for former merit his punishment was waived; he was ordered to manage grain funds, hunt remnant rebels, and disband the militia.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Shaanxi stragglers broke from the Southern Mountains along the plank roads; Qing raced to Guangyuan, sent men to negotiate, and they were slain; the court scolded his credulity, but spared him for past service and set him to provisions, mopping up remnants, and disbanding militia.

sentences.zh: 十年，事竣入覲，賜御製詩，有曰：「循吏清名遐邇傳，蜀民何幸見青天！

translations.literal: In the tenth year, when the work was finished he came to audience and was given an imperial poem, which read in part: "The honest official's fair name spreads far and near; how fortunate are Shu's people to see the blue sky!
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, duties done, he had audience and received an imperial poem that ran in part, "The upright magistrate's name travels far; how lucky are Shu's people to meet the blue sky!

sentences.zh: 誠心到處能和眾，本性從來不愛錢。」

translations.literal: Wherever his sincere heart goes he can harmonize the multitude; by nature he has never loved money."
translations.idiomatic: Where his honest heart goes the crowd is won; by nature he never loved cash."

sentences.zh: 時以異數榮之。

translations.literal: At the time this was regarded as a singular honor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time this was treated as a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 丁繼母憂，去官，服闋，授山西按察使，遷布政使。

translations.literal: He mourned his stepmother, left office, and after the mourning period was appointed Shanxi provincial surveillance commissioner and then provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his stepmother he left office; when mourning ended he became Shanxi provincial surveillance commissioner, then provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 忤巡撫初彭齡，劾其袒護屬吏，降四級，以從四品京堂用。

translations.literal: He clashed with Governor Chu Pengling, who impeached him for shielding subordinates; he was demoted four ranks and appointed a fourth-rank capital official.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed Governor Chu Pengling, who accused him of favoring subordinates; he was lowered four ranks and given a fourth-rank capital post.

sentences.zh: 清亦自陳不勝籓司之任，詔斥冒昧，降補刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: Qing also declared himself unfit for a provincial post; an edict rebuked his presumption and he was demoted to a clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Qing himself said he was unfit for a provincial post; the throne called him rash and reduced him to an outer-section clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 熱河新設理刑司員，以清往，邊方草創，多持大體，斷獄平允，蒙民亦以青天呼之。

translations.literal: Rehe had newly established a judicial post in the penal office; Qing was sent there; the frontier was newly organized, he often held to broad principles, judged cases fairly, and the Mongols also called him Blue Sky.
translations.idiomatic: Rehe had just set up a penal-office post; Qing was sent there; on a raw frontier he usually judged in broad spirit, decided cases fairly, and Mongols too called him Blue Sky.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授山東鹽運使。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Shandong salt commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was made Shandong salt commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十八年，河南教匪起，山東賊黨硃成良等應之，陷定陶、曹縣，巡撫同興恇懼，清自請將兵。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year teaching rebels rose in Henan; Shandong partisans such as Zhu Chengliang answered them, seized Dingtao and Cao County; Governor Tongxing was terrified, and Qing volunteered to lead troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Henan sect rebels rose; Shandong bands led by Zhu Chengliang joined in and took Dingtao and Cao County; Governor Tongxing panicked, and Qing asked to command troops.

sentences.zh: 承平久，兵習晏安，清躡草屩先之，以五百人敗賊於仿山，复定陶，又敗之於韓家廟，殪賊二千，進攻扈家集，縱火焚柵，賊突出皆死，誅賊首硃成良、王奇山，自滑縣奔至者並殲焉，兩閱月而事平。

translations.literal: After long peace the troops were soft; Qing went ahead in straw sandals; with five hundred men he defeated the rebels at Fang Mountain, recovered Dingtao, beat them again at Han Family Temple, killed two thousand rebels, attacked Huji Stockade, set fire to the palisade, and the rebels who rushed out all died; the chiefs Zhu Chengliang and Wang Qishan were executed, and those who had fled from Hua County were also wiped out; in two months the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Long peace had made the army slack; Qing led in straw sandals; with five hundred men he beat the rebels at Fang Mountain, retook Dingtao, routed them at Han Family Temple, killed two thousand, stormed Huji Stockade, burned the fence, and rebels who burst out all died; chiefs Zhu Chengliang and Wang Qishan were executed, fugitives from Hua County were destroyed, and in two months order returned.

sentences.zh: 賊初起時，煽惑甚眾，清先解散其脅從，成良勢孤不得逞，故得速定​​。

translations.literal: When the rebels first rose they had swayed a great crowd; Qing first dissolved their coerced followers, Chengliang was isolated and could not act, and so the matter was quickly settled.
translations.idiomatic: At first the rebels had drawn vast numbers; Qing first broke up their pressed followers, Chengliang stood alone and could not prevail, and the revolt was quickly crushed.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其以文職身先士卒，特詔褒獎，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him for a civil official who led from the front, issued a special commendation, and added provincial treasurer rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised a civil official who fought in the van, issued a special reward, and gave him provincial treasurer rank.

sentences.zh: 尋授雲南布政使，仍留舊任。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Yunnan provincial treasurer but kept at his old post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named Yunnan treasurer but remained at his former duty.

sentences.zh: 清性坦率，厭苛禮，不合於上官，又不耐簿書錢穀，遂乞病，上亦知之，改授山東登州鎮總兵，調曹州鎮。

translations.literal: Qing was frank by nature, disliked stiff ceremony, did not suit his superiors, and could not endure paperwork and revenue accounts; he asked to retire on grounds of illness, the emperor knew him well, changed his appointment to brigadier-general of Dengzhou Garrison in Shandong, then transferred him to Caozhou Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Frank by nature, weary of stiff ritual, ill-suited to superiors, and unable to bear ledgers and grain accounts, he pleaded illness; the emperor understood, made him brigadier of Dengzhou in Shandong, then moved him to Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，以老休致，命在籍食全俸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he retired for age; he was ordered to draw full salary while living at home.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 2 he retired on age and was allowed full salary at home.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒，賜祭葬，祀山東名宦，官其孫熾昌為兵部主事；

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died; funeral sacrifices were granted, he was entered in the temple of eminent officials of Shandong, and his grandson Chichang was given a post as a secretary in the Ministry of War;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died; state rites were granted, he was honored in Shandong's temple of worthy officials, and his grandson Chichang was given a secretaryship in the Ministry of War;

sentences.zh: 瑩，舉人。

translations.literal: Ying became a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: his grandson Ying became a provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 傅鼐，字重庵，順天宛平人，原籍浙江山陰。

translations.literal: Fu Nai, courtesy name Chong'an, was a native of Wanping in Shuntian, originally from Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Nai, styled Chong'an, was from Wanping in Shuntian, with ancestral roots in Shanyin, Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 由吏員入貲為府經歷，發雲南，擢寧洱知縣。

translations.literal: Entering through the clerical track by purchase of office, he became a prefectural clerk, was sent to Yunnan, and was promoted magistrate of Ning'er.
translations.idiomatic: He entered by purchase as a prefectural clerk, was posted to Yunnan, and rose to magistrate of Ning'er.

sentences.zh: 乾隆末，福康安徵苗疆，調赴湖南軍營司餉運，晉秩同知直隸州，賜花翎。

translations.literal: At the end of the Qianlong reign Fuk'anggan campaigned in the Miao frontier; Nai was transferred to the Hunan army camp to manage supply transport, was advanced to subprefect of Zhili Prefecture, and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of Qianlong, Fuk'anggan campaigned in the Miao country; Nai was sent to the Hunan army to manage supplies, advanced to subprefect of Zhili Prefecture, and given the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，授鳳凰廳同知。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing he was appointed subprefect of Fenghuang Department.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 1 he was made subprefect of Fenghuang Department.

sentences.zh: 治當苗衝，會大軍移徵湖北教匪，降苗要求苗地歸苗，當事議允之。

translations.literal: His jurisdiction lay on the Miao frontier; the main army moved to suppress the Hubei teaching rebels, pacified Miao demanded Miao land returned to Miao, and the authorities agreed.
translations.idiomatic: He governed a Miao frontier sector; when the main force marched against Hubei sect rebels, pacified Miao demanded their lands back and officials agreed.

sentences.zh: 鼐知愈撫且愈驕，乃招流亡，團丁壯，於要害築碉堡，防苗出沒。

translations.literal: Nai knew that the more they were appeased the prouder they grew; he gathered refugees, mustered able men, and built stockaded forts at strategic points to block Miao raids.
translations.idiomatic: Nai saw that indulgence only bred arrogance; he gathered exiles, drilled strong youths, and built stockades at passes to block Miao incursions.

sentences.zh: 苗以死力來攻，且戰且修，閱三年而碉堡成。

translations.literal: The Miao attacked with all their strength; he fought while building, and after three years the stockades were complete.
translations.idiomatic: Miao attacked with deadly force; he fought while building, and in three years the forts stood complete.

sentences.zh: 有哨台以守望，砲台以御敵，邊牆相接百餘裡。

translations.literal: There were watch towers for lookout and gun platforms to repel the enemy, with connecting border walls for more than a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Watch towers scanned the hills, gun platforms met attacks, and border walls linked for more than a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 每警，哨台舉銃角，婦女、牲畜立歸堡，環數十里皆戒嚴。

translations.literal: Whenever alarm came, the watch towers fired signal guns; women, livestock, and all immediately entered the forts, and for dozens of li around strict guard was kept.
translations.idiomatic: At every alarm towers fired signal guns; women and stock were rushed into forts, and for tens of li all stood on guard.

sentences.zh: 四年，擒苗酋吳陳受，加知府銜。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Miao chief Wu Chenshou was captured and Nai was given prefectural rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Miao chief Wu Chenshou was taken and Nai received prefectural rank.

sentences.zh: 巡撫姜晟疏薦鼐能勝艱鉅，方治鎮筸一帶荒田，均給丁壯，請俟事竣送部。

translations.literal: Governor Jiang Sheng memorialized that Nai could bear heavy tasks; he was reclaiming wasteland around Zhengan, distributing it evenly to able men, and asked that he be sent to the ministry after the work was done.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Jiang Sheng praised Nai for heavy duties; he was opening wasteland around Zhengan and allotting plots to strong men, asking to present him to the ministry when finished.

sentences.zh: 時鎮筸左、右營黑苗最為邊患，五年，跴金塘苗出掠瀘溪，偕總兵富志那夜分三路搗其巢，伏兵隘路苟岩要擊，痛殲之，斃首逆吳尚保，苗始奪氣。

translations.literal: At that time the Black Miao of the left and right camps of Zhengan were the worst border trouble; in the fifth year Jintang Miao raided Luxi; with Brigadier Fuzhina he divided into three routes by night and stormed their lair, ambushed them at the pass of Gouyan, inflicted a heavy defeat, killed the ringleader Wu Shangbao, and the Miao lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Then Black Miao of Zhengan's left and right camps were the worst scourge; in the fifth year Jintang Miao raided Luxi; with Brigadier Fuzhina he struck their nest in three night columns, ambushed them at Gouyan Pass, crushed them, killed ringleader Wu Shangbao, and Miao morale broke.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉獎，命在任食知府俸。

translations.literal: An edict praised him and ordered that while in post he draw a prefect's salary.
translations.idiomatic: The throne commended him and let him draw a prefect's pay while remaining subprefect.

sentences.zh: 六年，貴州苗复亂，湖南環苗地東、南、北三面七百餘裡，其西二百餘裡接貴州，未設備。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Guizhou Miao rebelled again; Hunan on the east, south, and north of the Miao country stretched more than seven hundred li, while the west for more than two hundred li bordered Guizhou and had no defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Guizhou Miao rose again; Hunan's Miao lands ran seven hundred-odd li on east, south, and north, while two hundred li west against Guizhou were undefended.

sentences.zh: 石峴苗煽十四寨糾湖南苗叛，鼐率鄉勇千五百馳赴銅仁。

translations.literal: Shixian Miao stirred fourteen stockades to join Hunan Miao in revolt; Nai led fifteen hundred militia in a rush to Tongren.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian Miao roused fourteen stockades with Hunan Miao; Nai raced to Tongren with fifteen hundred militia.

sentences.zh: 貴州巡撫伊桑阿以招撫戡定上聞，各寨實尚沸然，槍械未繳。

translations.literal: Guizhou Governor Yisang'a reported pacification by inducement to the throne, but in fact every stockade still seethed and firearms had not been surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou Governor Yisang'a reported pacification to the court, yet stockades still boiled and guns were not turned in.

sentences.zh: 總督琅玕至，急檄鼐會剿崖屯溝，黔兵攻其前，鼐夜由山徑入，連破五巢。

translations.literal: Governor-General Langgale arrived and urgently ordered Nai to join the campaign at Yaitungou; Guizhou troops attacked in front while Nai entered by a mountain path at night and took five lairs in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Langgale came, urgently summoned Nai to Yaitungou; Guizhou troops struck in front while Nai entered by a night mountain trail and broke five nests in a row.

sentences.zh: 上下湖山峽尤險，夜分兵圍攻，至次日克之，火其寨。

translations.literal: The upper and lower Hushan Gorge was especially perilous; troops surrounded it at night and took it the next day, burning the stockade.
translations.idiomatic: The upper and lower Hushan Gorge was most dangerous; troops invested it by night, took it next day, and burned the camp.

sentences.zh: 三日中盡破諸寨，殲苗二千有奇。

translations.literal: Within three days every stockade was broken and more than two thousand Miao were killed.
translations.idiomatic: In three days all stockades fell and more than two thousand Miao were killed.

sentences.zh: 仿湖南法，建碉堡守之。

translations.literal: Following the Hunan method, he built stockaded forts to hold the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He copied Hunan's method and built stockades to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 伊桑阿因冒功誤邊伏法，錄鼐功，加道銜，總理邊務，並命以苗疆道員用。

translations.literal: Yisang'a was executed for false merit that harmed the border; Nai's merit was recorded, he was given circuit rank, put in charge of frontier affairs, and ordered to serve as a Miao frontier intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yisang'a was executed for boasting of merit and harming the border; Nai was rewarded with circuit rank, overall frontier charge, and appointment as Miao frontier intendant.

sentences.zh: 七年，丁父憂，詔鼐辦理邊防善後，民、苗悅服，難易生手，命留任。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he mourned his father; an edict ordered Nai to manage frontier defense and aftermath; people and Miao were content; the work was hard for a newcomer, so he was kept in post.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he mourned his father; the court kept him to settle frontier defense—people and Miao were loyal, the task too delicate for a novice—so he stayed in office.

sentences.zh: 初，鼐建議遷永綏城於花園，副將營於茶洞，而貴州方藉永綏為聲援，尼其事。

translations.literal: Earlier Nai had proposed moving Yongshui city to Huayuan and the vice commander's camp to Chadong, but Guizhou relied on Yongshui as support and blocked the plan.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier urged moving Yongshui city to Huayuan and the vice commander's camp to Chadong, but Guizhou needed Yongshui as a prop and blocked it.

sentences.zh: 至是詔琅玕察奏，乃赴銅仁面陳永綏孤懸苗中，形如釜底，有二難、三可慮；

translations.literal: Now an edict ordered Langgale to investigate and report; Nai went to Tongren and stated in person that Yongshui stood alone among Miao like the bottom of a cauldron, with two difficulties and three points to weigh;
translations.idiomatic: Now Langgale was told to investigate; Nai went to Tongren and argued that Yongshui hung alone among Miao like a pot's bottom, with two hardships and three concerns;

sentences.zh: 並請移湖南守備於貴州邊境螺螄堡，以為犄角，乃決議移之。

translations.literal: he also asked to move Hunan's garrison commander to Luoxi Fort on the Guizhou border as a flank, and the move was decided.
translations.idiomatic: he also asked to shift a Hunan garrison to Luoxi Fort on the Guizhou line as a pincer, and the move was approved.

sentences.zh: 既而群苗率眾來爭，鼐率鄉勇深入，苗大集，環之數重，以奇計突圍出。

translations.literal: Soon Miao gathered in force to contest it; Nai led militia deep in; Miao massed and ringed him many deep, but he broke out by a stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Miao mustered to fight the move; Nai led militia deep inside; they surrounded him in many rings, yet he broke out by a ruse.

sentences.zh: 尋議勒繳槍械，苗酋石崇四等抗命，並阻丈田，十年，與其黨石貴銀糾眾數千來犯，敗之夯都河，追至孟陽岡，殲賊甚眾，生擒石崇四、石貴銀。

translations.literal: When collection of firearms was enforced, chiefs such as Shi Chongsi resisted and blocked land survey; in the tenth year he and his follower Shi Guiyin gathered thousands to attack; Nai defeated them at Handu River, pursued to Mengyang Ridge, killed many, and captured Shi Chongsi and Shi Guiyin alive.
translations.idiomatic: When guns were ordered in, chiefs like Shi Chongsi resisted and blocked land measure; in the tenth year he and Shi Guiyin raised thousands; Nai beat them at Handu River, chased to Mengyang Ridge, killed heavily, and took both chiefs alive.

sentences.zh: 是役因賊戕良苗，故得用苗兵深入，戰月餘，破寨十六，餘皆乞降，永綏苗遂平。

translations.literal: In this campaign, because the rebels had killed loyal Miao, he could use Miao troops in depth; fighting more than a month he broke sixteen stockades; the rest begged surrender, and Yongshui Miao were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Because rebels had killed loyal Miao, he could use Miao soldiers deep in the hills; after a month he stormed sixteen stockades; the rest surrendered and Yongshui was calm.

sentences.zh: 廳屬高都、兩頭羊二寨皆震懾，無敢抗。

translations.literal: Gaodu and Liangtouyang stockades under the department were awed and dared not resist.
translations.idiomatic: Department stockades Gaodu and Liangtouyang were cowed and dared not resist.

sentences.zh: 事聞，予優敘，擢辰沅永靖道。

translations.literal: When the report reached court he received preferential reward and was promoted intendant of Chen-Yuan-Yong-Jing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave him preferential reward and made him intendant of Chen-Yuan-Yong-Jing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 鼐治苗專用雕剿法，大小百戰，所用僅鄉勇數千。

translations.literal: In governing the Miao Nai relied solely on the stockade-suppression method; in battles large and small, more than a hundred, he used only a few thousand militia.
translations.idiomatic: Governing Miao, Nai relied wholly on stockade warfare; in a hundred-odd fights large and small he used only a few thousand militia.

sentences.zh: 苗人於穹山峭壁驀越如平地，無部伍行列，伏箐中從暗擊明，銃銳且長，隨山起伏，多命中。

translations.literal: The Miao on dome-like mountains and sheer cliffs leaped as on level ground, without ranks or formations; lying in ambush in thickets they struck from darkness against light; their muskets were sharp and long, rising and falling with the hills, and often hit their mark.
translations.idiomatic: On vaulted peaks and cliff faces Miao moved as if on flat ground, without ranks; hiding in thickets they struck from cover; their long muskets followed the hills and rarely missed.

sentences.zh: 鼐因苗地用苗技訓練士卒，囊沙輕走，習藤牌閃躍，狹路則用短兵。

translations.literal: Nai therefore trained his soldiers in Miao country by Miao methods: carrying sand to run lightly, practicing rattan-shield dodging and leaping, and using short weapons on narrow paths.
translations.idiomatic: In Miao terrain he drilled troops Miao-style—sand-filled packs for light marching, rattan-shield leaps, short blades on narrow trails.

sentences.zh: 每戰後輒嚴汰，數年始得精卒千，號「飛隊」，風雨不亂行列，遺資道路無反顧，甘苦與共，是以能致死。

translations.literal: After every battle he strictly culled the ranks; only after several years did he obtain a thousand elite troops, called the "Flying Corps," who kept formation in wind and rain, left supplies on the road without turning back, shared hardship and comfort, and thus could fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: After each fight he culled weak men; years later he had a thousand elites, the "Flying Corps," steady in storm, who abandoned baggage without looking back, shared every hardship, and would die where they stood.

sentences.zh: 先是議興屯田，上書巡撫高杞曰：「防邊之道，兵民相輔。

translations.literal: Earlier, when garrison farming was under discussion, he memorialized Governor Gao Qi: "The way to defend a border is for soldiers and civilians to support each other.
translations.idiomatic: When garrison farming was debated he wrote Governor Gao Qi: "Border defense depends on soldiers and people aiding each other.

sentences.zh: 湖南苗疆，環以鳳凰、永綏、乾州、古丈坪、保靖五廳縣，犬牙相錯，營汛相距各數里。

translations.literal: The Miao frontier of Hunan is ringed by the five departments and counties of Fenghuang, Yongshui, Qianzhou, Guzhangping, and Baojing, interlocking like dog teeth; garrisons and posts stand a few li apart.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan's Miao frontier is girdled by Fenghuang, Yongshui, Qianzhou, Guzhangping, and Baojing, jigsawed together with posts a few li apart.

sentences.zh: 元年班師後苗擾如故，鼐竭心籌之，制勝無如碉堡。

translations.literal: After the army withdrew in the first year the Miao troubled the border as before; Nai gave his whole mind to planning, and there was no better way to prevail than stockaded forts.
translations.idiomatic: After the first-year withdrawal Miao raids continued; Nai planned tirelessly and found stockades the surest answer.

sentences.zh: 募丁壯數千，與苗從事。

translations.literal: He recruited several thousand able-bodied men to contend with the Miao.
translations.idiomatic: He raised several thousand stout men to fight Miao head-on.

sentences.zh: 來則痛擊，去則修邊，前戈矛，後邪許。

translations.literal: When they came he struck hard; when they left he repaired the border—spears in front, work songs behind.
translations.idiomatic: When Miao came he hit hard; when they left he built walls—spears ahead, hauling chants behind.

sentences.zh: 得險即守，寸步而前，然後苗銳挫望絕。

translations.literal: Seizing every strong point he held it and advanced inch by inch, until the Miao's edge was broken and their hope cut off.
translations.idiomatic: He seized every defile, held it, crept forward, until Miao daring broke and hope died.

sentences.zh: 湖南自乙卯二載用兵，耗帑七百餘萬。

translations.literal: Hunan since the yimao years had fought two years of war and spent more than seven million taels of treasury funds.
translations.idiomatic: Since the yimao campaigns Hunan had spent over seven million taels in two years of war.

sentences.zh: 國家經費有常，頑苗叛服無定。

translations.literal: State revenue has its fixed limits, while stubborn Miao rebel and submit without rule.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial funds are fixed, yet stubborn Miao sway between revolt and peace.

sentences.zh: 募勇不得不散，則碉堡不得不虛；

translations.literal: When hired braves must be dispersed, the stockades cannot but stand empty;
translations.idiomatic: When militia must be dismissed, stockades must go empty;

sentences.zh: 後患不得不慮，則自圖不得不亟。

translations.literal: when future trouble cannot but be feared, self-reliance cannot but be urgent.
translations.idiomatic: when future trouble is feared, self-sufficiency cannot wait.

sentences.zh: 通力合作，且耕且戰，所以招亡拯患也。

translations.literal: Joining strength to cooperate, farming while fighting—this is how to win back the lost and save the afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: Shared labor, farming and fighting together, wins back the lost and relieves distress.

sentences.zh: 均田屯丁，自養自衛，所以一勞永逸也。

translations.literal: Equalizing land among garrison farmers who feed and defend themselves—this is how to settle the matter once for all.
translations.idiomatic: Land shared among garrison farmers who feed and guard themselves settles the border for good.

sentences.zh: 相其距苗遠近、碉堡疏密，為屯田多少：鳳凰廳碉堡八百，需丁四千輪守，並留千人備戰，需田三萬餘畝；

translations.literal: According to distance from the Miao and density of stockades, the amount of garrison land was set: Fenghuang Department had eight hundred stockades, needing four thousand men in rotation to guard them, with another thousand held in reserve for battle, requiring more than thirty thousand mu of fields;
translations.idiomatic: By distance from Miao and density of forts he set acreage: Fenghuang's eight hundred stockades needed four thousand rotating guards plus a thousand reserves—over thirty thousand mu;

sentences.zh: 乾州廳碉堡九十餘，守丁八百，屯田三千餘畝；

translations.literal: Qianzhou Department had more than ninety stockades, eight hundred garrison men, and more than three thousand mu of garrison fields;
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhou's ninety-odd forts needed eight hundred men and three thousand mu;

sentences.zh: 保靖縣碉堡四十餘，守丁三百，屯田千五百餘畝；

translations.literal: Baojing County had more than forty stockades, three hundred garrison men, and more than fifteen hundred mu;
translations.idiomatic: Baojing's forty-odd forts needed three hundred men and fifteen hundred mu;

sentences.zh: 古丈坪廳苗馴，止設碉堡十餘，守丁百，屯田五百餘畝；

translations.literal: Guzhangping Department had tame Miao and needed only a dozen or so stockades, a hundred garrison men, and more than five hundred mu;
translations.idiomatic: Tame Miao at Guzhangping needed only a dozen forts, a hundred men, five hundred mu;

sentences.zh: 永綏廳新建碉堡百餘，留勇丁二千，亦屯田萬畝：而後邊無餘隙，環苗以成圈圍之勢，峻國防、省國計也。

translations.literal: Yongshui Department newly built more than a hundred stockades and kept two thousand brave garrison men, also garrisoning ten thousand mu of fields: thus the rear border had no gap, and encircling the Miao formed a ring of containment—strengthening national defense and saving state expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Yongshui added a hundred forts and two thousand braves with ten thousand mu—closing gaps, ringing Miao in a cordon that hardened the frontier and saved the treasury.

sentences.zh: 異族逼處，非碉堡無以固，碉堡非勇丁無以守，勇丁非屯田無以贍。

translations.literal: With alien peoples pressing close, without stockades there is no solidity; without brave garrison men stockades cannot be held; without garrison fields the brave cannot be fed.
translations.idiomatic: Alien neighbors require forts; forts require garrison men; garrison men require land.

sentences.zh: 邊民瀕近鋒鏑，固原割世業而保身家；

translations.literal: Border people on the edge of battle naturally would rather cut off hereditary estates to save their persons;
translations.idiomatic: Border folk under the sword would surrender ancestral fields to save their lives;

sentences.zh: 後路同資屏蔽，亦樂捐有餘以補不足。

translations.literal: those in the rear who share in the shield are also glad to give their surplus to supply what is lacking.
translations.idiomatic: inland counties glad to give surplus to cover shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 所募土丁，非其子弟即其親族。

translations.literal: The local militia recruited were either their sons or their kin.
translations.idiomatic: Recruits were sons or kin, not strangers.

sentences.zh: 距邊稍遠者，仍佃本戶輸租，視古來屯戍以客卒雜處，勢燕越矣。

translations.literal: Those a little farther from the border still rented from their own households and paid rent, unlike ancient garrison practice of mixing outside soldiers with locals—the situation was as different as Yan from Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Men farther back still farmed family plots and paid rent—unlike old garrisons of mixed outsiders, a world apart.

sentences.zh: 與其一旦散數千驍健無業子弟流為盜賊，何如收駕輕就熟之用而不費大帑一錢？

translations.literal: Rather than one day dispersing several thousand fierce, jobless young men who would become bandits, is it not better to employ ready skills and spend not a single large coin from the treasury?
translations.idiomatic: Better employ trained youths than disband thousands who would turn bandit—without one treasury coin.

sentences.zh: 惟執事圖之！」

translations.literal: I beg Your Excellency to consider this!"
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Excellency to act on this!"

sentences.zh: 於是收叛產分給無業窮苗佃種。

translations.literal: Thereupon rebel property was collected and distributed to landless poor Miao for tenant farming.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel lands were then divided among landless Miao tenants.

sentences.zh: 自擒石崇四，餘匪原返侵地，永綏得萬餘畝，乾州、鳳凰二廳次之，乃續墾沿邊隙地二萬畝，曰「官墾田」，贖苗質民田萬餘畝，曰「官贖田」。

translations.literal: After Shi Chongsi was captured, remaining bandits returned invaded land; Yongshui gained more than ten thousand mu, Qianzhou and Fenghuang departments next; then he continued reclaiming more than twenty thousand mu of border gaps, called "official reclaimed land," and redeemed more than ten thousand mu of civilian land held in pawn by Miao, called "official redemption land."
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Chongsi's capture, invaders' lands returned; Yongshui gained ten thousand mu, then Qianzhou and Fenghuang; he reclaimed twenty thousand mu as "official reclaimed land" and redeemed ten thousand mu pawned to Miao as "official redemption land."

sentences.zh: 以廩屯官授屯長，給老幼，籌補助，備犒賞，暨歲修城堡、神祠、學校、育嬰、養濟諸費。

translations.literal: From granary garrison fields he appointed garrison chiefs, supported old and young, planned subsidies, prepared rewards, and covered yearly repair of forts, shrines, schools, orphanages, and poor relief.
translations.idiomatic: Granary fields funded chiefs, the aged, subsidies, rewards, and yearly repairs to forts, shrines, schools, orphanages, and poorhouses.

sentences.zh: 復以兵威勒交苗佔民田三萬五千餘畝，苗自獻田七千餘畝。

translations.literal: By military pressure he also compelled Miao to return more than thirty-five thousand mu of civilian land they had occupied, and Miao themselves offered more than seven thousand mu.
translations.idiomatic: By force he made Miao return thirty-five thousand mu seized from civilians; Miao voluntarily gave seven thousand more.

sentences.zh: 其經費田則佃租變價，屯丁田則附碉躬耕，訓練講武，設屯田守備掌之，轄於兵備道。

translations.literal: Revenue fields were rented out and sold; garrison men's fields were farmed beside the stockades with military drill; a garrison-field commandant was established under the military intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue plots were leased or sold; garrison men farmed beside forts and drilled; a garrison commandant answered to the military intendant.

sentences.zh: 屯政舉，使兵農為一以相衛，民、苗為二以相安。

translations.literal: When garrison policy was established, soldiers and farmers became one to guard each other, while civilians and Miao remained two groups living in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison policy united soldier and farmer for mutual defense while keeping civilian and Miao separate but at peace.

sentences.zh: 與官及兵民約曰：「毋擅入苗寨，毋稍役苗夫。」

translations.literal: With officials and soldiers and civilians he made a pact: "Do not enter Miao stockades without permission; do not lightly impress Miao laborers."
translations.idiomatic: He pledged officials and troops: "Enter no Miao village unbidden; press no Miao labor."

sentences.zh: 與苗約曰：「毋巫鬼椎牛群飲以糜財，毋挾槍矛尋睚眥釀釁。」

translations.literal: With the Miao he made a pact: "Do not waste wealth on shamans, ox sacrifices, and group drinking; do not carry guns and spears to settle grudges and stir trouble."
translations.idiomatic: To Miao he pledged: "No spirit rites, ox feasts, or drinking bouts that drain wealth; no guns for private feuds."

sentences.zh: 請乾、鳳、永、保四廳編立邊字號，廣鄉試中額一名；

translations.literal: He asked that the four departments of Qian, Feng, Yong, and Bao establish a frontier examination quota with one added provincial graduate;
translations.idiomatic: He sought a frontier exam quota for Qian, Feng, Yong, and Bao with one added graduate slot;

sentences.zh: 苗生編立田字號，加中額一名，苗益感奮。

translations.literal: Miao students were given a separate "field" quota with one added pass, and the Miao were all the more stirred to effort.
translations.idiomatic: Miao students gained a "field" quota with an extra pass, stirring them to study.

sentences.zh: 十三年，屯務竣，入覲，詔曰：「傅鼐任苗疆十餘年，鋤莠安良，興利除弊，建碉堡千有餘所，屯田十二萬餘畝，收卹難民十餘萬戶，練兵八千人，收繳苗寨兵器四萬餘件；

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when garrison affairs were complete, he came to audience; an edict said: "Fu Nai has served on the Miao frontier more than ten years, rooting out the wicked and settling the good, promoting benefit and removing harm, building more than a thousand stockades, garrisoning more than a hundred and twenty thousand mu, receiving and succoring more than a hundred thousand refugee households, drilling eight thousand troops, and collecting more than forty thousand weapons from Miao stockades;
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, garrison work done, he had audience; the edict read: "Fu Nai served the Miao frontier over ten years, rooting evil, aiding the good, building a thousand forts, garrisoning a hundred twenty thousand mu, succoring a hundred thousand refugee households, drilling eight thousand men, collecting forty thousand Miao weapons;

sentences.zh: 又多方化導，設書院六，義學百，近日苗民向學，革面革心。

translations.literal: he has also guided them in many ways, established six academies and a hundred charity schools; recently Miao people turn to learning and reform heart and face.
translations.idiomatic: he guided them, founded six academies and a hundred charity schools; Miao now study and reform.

sentences.zh: 朕久聞其任勞任怨，不顧身家。

translations.literal: We have long heard that he bears labor and blame without regard for self or family.
translations.idiomatic: We long heard he bore every burden without regard for self.

sentences.zh: 今召見，果安詳諳練，明白誠實，洵為傑出之才，堪為岩疆保障。

translations.literal: Now on meeting him, he is indeed calm, skilled, clear, and honest—a truly outstanding talent fit to guard a rugged frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting him, he is calm, skilled, honest—a talent fit to guard rugged borders.

sentences.zh: 其加按察使銜，以風有位。」

translations.literal: Let him be given vice censor rank to set an example for those in office."
translations.idiomatic: Grant vice censor rank to inspire other officials."

sentences.zh: 十四年，擢湖南按察使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted Hunan vice censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he became Hunan vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 苗人籥留，命每年秋一赴苗疆撫慰邊人。

translations.literal: The Miao begged with pipes that he stay; he was ordered to visit the Miao frontier once each autumn to comfort the border people.
translations.idiomatic: Miao pleaded with pipes for him to stay; the court ordered one autumn visit yearly to comfort the frontier.

sentences.zh: 鼐在苗疆，設木匭於門，訴者投牒其中，夜出閱之，黎明起視事，剖決立盡。

translations.literal: While on the Miao frontier Nai set a wooden box at his gate; complainants put petitions in it; he read them at night, rose at dawn to hear cases, and decided them on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontier he placed a petition box at his gate, read filings by night, judged at dawn, and finished every case.

sentences.zh: 兵民白事，直至榻前。

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians reporting affairs came straight to his couch.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians brought business even to his bedside.

sentences.zh: 及為按察使，一如同知時。

translations.literal: When he became vice censor he was the same as when he had been subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: As vice censor he lived as simply as when he was subprefect.

sentences.zh: 下無壅情，事無不舉。

translations.literal: Below there was no blocked information; nothing failed to be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing was hidden from him; nothing went undone.

sentences.zh: 十五年，兼署布政使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he also acted as provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he acted as provincial treasurer as well.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒於官，仁宗深悼惜，詔謂：「倚畀方隆，正欲簡任疆寄。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died in office; Emperor Renzong deeply mourned and an edict said: "Our reliance on him was just rising; we were about to select him for a frontier post.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he died in office; Renzong mourned deeply: "We had just begun to rely on him for a frontier post.

sentences.zh: 加恩贈巡撫銜，照贈官賜卹，賜祭一壇。」

translations.literal: Grace was added: posthumous rank of governor, funeral gifts according to the rank granted, and one sacrificial altar."
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given governor rank, full mourning honors, and one state sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 苗疆建專祠，祀湖南名宦。

translations.literal: A special temple was built on the Miao frontier, and he was entered in the temple of eminent officials of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: A frontier temple was raised and he entered Hunan's hall of worthy officials.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，追諡壯肅。

translations.literal: In the Guangxu period he was posthumously given the posthumous name Zhuangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangxu he received the posthumous name Zhuangsu.

sentences.zh: 初，鼐排眾議以事攻剿，為大吏所惎，將中以開邊釁罪。

translations.literal: Earlier, Nai had gone against common opinion to pursue attack and suppression; great officials were jealous and were about to charge him with the crime of provoking a border quarrel.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Nai defied opinion to fight Miao; superiors envied him and nearly charged him with provoking the border.

sentences.zh: 監司阿意，旁掣其肘，鎮筸總兵富志那獨保全之。

translations.literal: Circuit intendants flattered their superiors and hampered him from the side; only Zhengan Brigadier Fuzhina alone protected him.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit men flattered superiors and hindered him; only Brigadier Fuzhina shielded him.

sentences.zh: 富志那從征金川，習知山碉設險之利，鼐實從受之，卒以成功。

translations.literal: Fuzhina had campaigned in Jinchuan and knew the advantage of mountain stockades and terrain; Nai in fact learned from him and finally succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhina, veteran of Jinchuan, knew mountain stockades; Nai learned from him and prevailed.

sentences.zh: 鼐歿後，二妾寡居，饣於粥不給，其廉操尤著雲。

translations.literal: After Nai's death his two concubines lived as widows and could not get enough gruel; his frugality was especially renowned.
translations.idiomatic: After his death two concubines lived in poverty on thin gruel—proof of his integrity.

sentences.zh: 嚴如熤，字炳文，湖南溆浦人。

translations.literal: Yan Ruyi, courtesy name Bingwen, was a native of Xupu in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ruyi, styled Bingwen, came from Xupu in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 年十三，補諸生，舉優貢。

translations.literal: At thirteen he became a licentiate and was selected as an outstanding tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he became a licentiate and passed as an outstanding tribute student.

sentences.zh: 研究輿圖、兵法、星卜之書，尤留心兵事。

translations.literal: He studied books on geography, military science, and astrology, and paid special attention to military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He studied geography, strategy, and divination, but cared most for military affairs.

sentences.zh: 乾隆六十年，貴州苗亂，湖南巡撫姜晟闢佐幕，上平苗​​議十二事，言宜急复乾州，進永綏，與保靖、松桃、鎮筸聲勢可通。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year of Qianlong, when the Guizhou Miao rebelled, Hunan Governor Jiang Sheng opened a staff post for him; he submitted twelve proposals for pacifying the Miao, saying that Qianzhou should quickly be recovered, Yongshui advanced, and contact made with Baojing, Songtao, and Zhengan so that their forces could link.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 60, when Guizhou Miao rebelled, Governor Jiang Sheng took him on staff; his twelve proposals urged recovering Qianzhou, advancing Yongshui, and linking Baojing, Songtao, and Zhengan.

sentences.zh: 攻乾州道瀘溪，必先得大小章。

translations.literal: To attack Qianzhou by way of Luxi, one must first win Daxiaozhang.
translations.idiomatic: The Luxi route to Qianzhou required winning Daxiaozhang first.

sentences.zh: 大小章者，故土司遺民，名曰仡佬，驍健，與苗世仇。

translations.literal: Daxiaozhang were remnant people of the old native chieftains, called Gelao, fierce fighters and hereditary enemies of the Miao.
translations.idiomatic: Daxiaozhang were Gelao descendants of old chiefs, fierce and sworn enemies of Miao.

sentences.zh: 如熤募能仡佬語者往，開示利害，挾其酋六人出，推誠與同臥起，乃送質，率其屬陽投乾州為內應，約一舉破賊，因黔師牽掣未果。

translations.literal: Ruyi recruited men who could speak Gelao, went to explain advantage and harm, brought out six of their chiefs, treated them with sincerity and shared sleeping and rising, then sent hostages; they led their followers to pretend submission to Qianzhou as inner collaborators, agreeing to break the rebels in one stroke, but because Guizhou troops were tied down it did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyi sent Gelao speakers, won six chiefs, lived among them in trust, took hostages, and won them as Qianzhou insiders—but Guizhou troops were tied down and the plan stalled.

sentences.zh: 次年，卒賴其眾，救兩鎮兵於河溪。

translations.literal: The next year he finally relied on their force to rescue two garrison commands at Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Next year their men rescued two commands at Hexi.

sentences.zh: 後復平隴，戰花園，皆為軍鋒。

translations.literal: Later again at Pinglong and fighting at Huayuan, he was always in the army's van.
translations.idiomatic: He later fought at Pinglong and Huayuan always in the van.

sentences.zh: 大小章於大府檄或不受，必得如熤手書始行雲。

translations.literal: Daxiaozhang might not obey a grand coordinator's order, but would act only on receiving Ruyi's own letter.
translations.idiomatic: Daxiaozhang ignored grand coordinators but obeyed Ruyi's personal letters.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年，舉孝廉方正。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiaqing he was recommended as filial and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 5 he was named filial and incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 廷試平定川、楚、陝三省方略策，如熤對幾萬言，略謂：「軍興數載，師老財匱。

translations.literal: In the palace examination on strategy for pacifying Sichuan, Hubei, and Shaanxi, Ruyi answered in tens of thousands of words, saying in summary: "The army has been raised several years; the troops are weary and funds exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace exam on pacifying Sichuan, Hubei, and Shaanxi he wrote tens of thousands of words opening: "Years of war have exhausted troops and treasury.

sentences.zh: 以數万罷憊之眾，與猾賊追逐數千里長林深谷中。

translations.literal: With tens of thousands of worn-out men chasing crafty bandits for thousands of li through long forests and deep valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of spent men chase crafty rebels thousands of li through forest and gorge.

sentences.zh: 投誠之賊，無地安置，則已降复亂；

translations.literal: Bandits who have surrendered have no place to settle, then those who have submitted rebel again;
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered rebels with nowhere to go rise again;

sentences.zh: 流離之民，生活無資，則良亦從亂。

translations.literal: displaced people with no means to live also join the disorder even when they were good.
translations.idiomatic: Homeless refugees without livelihood join the chaos;

sentences.zh: 鄉勇戍卒，多遊手募充。

translations.literal: Militia and garrison soldiers are mostly idlers recruited to fill the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Militia and garrison men are mostly hired idlers.

sentences.zh: 慮一旦兵撤餉停，則反思延亂。

translations.literal: Fearing that once troops are withdrawn and pay stops, they will again think of prolonging the chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that when troops withdraw and pay stops they will prolong war for profit.

sentences.zh: 如此，則亂何由弭？

translations.literal: In such a case, how can disorder be quelled?
translations.idiomatic: How then can order return?

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為莫若仿古屯田之法。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks nothing is better than the ancient garrison-farming method.
translations.idiomatic: I foolishly think nothing is better than adopting the ancient garrison-farming method.

sentences.zh: 三省自遭蹂躪，叛亡各產不下億萬畝，舉流民降賊之無歸、鄉勇戍卒之無業者，悉編入屯，團練捍衛，計可養勝兵數十萬。

translations.literal: The three provinces, since being trampled, have rebel and fugitive lands amounting to no less than hundreds of millions of mu; gather homeless refugees, surrendered bandits without refuge, and jobless militia and garrison men, enroll them all in garrisons, drill and defend them, and it is estimated that several hundred thousand victorious troops can be maintained.
translations.idiomatic: Trampled provinces hold endless idle land; enroll refugees, surrendered rebels, and jobless militia in garrisons to maintain hundreds of thousands of troops.

sentences.zh: 餉省而兵增，化盜為民，計無逾此。」

translations.literal: Pay is saved while troops increase; turning bandits into civilians—no plan surpasses this."
translations.idiomatic: Pay falls while strength rises—turning bandits into farmers—nothing better."

sentences.zh: 仁宗親擢第一。

translations.literal: The Emperor Renzong personally placed him first.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong ranked him first.

sentences.zh: 次日，召詣軍機處詢屯政，复條上十二事。

translations.literal: The next day he was summoned to the Grand Council to be questioned on garrison policy, and again submitted twelve items in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the Grand Council questioned him on garrison policy; he submitted twelve detailed points.

sentences.zh: 召見，以知縣發陝西。

translations.literal: On audience he was sent to Shaanxi as magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Shaanxi as magistrate.

sentences.zh: 下其疏於三省大吏，令採行。

translations.literal: His memorial was sent down to the great officials of the three provinces with orders to adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial went to the three provinces with orders to adopt it.

sentences.zh: 六年，補洵陽，縣在萬山中，與湖北邊界相錯，兵賊往來如織。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed to Xunyang; the county lay among ten thousand mountains, its border interlocking with Hubei, and soldiers and bandits came and went like weaving.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he took Xunyang, a county lost in mountains where Hubei borders crossed and troops and rebels shuttled constantly.

sentences.zh: 時方厲行堅壁清野，如熤於築堡練團，措置尤力。

translations.literal: At that time the strict "clear the fields" policy was enforced; Ruyi was especially forceful in building forts and drilling militia.
translations.idiomatic: Strict "clear the fields" policy ruled; Ruyi built forts and drilled militia with special force.

sentences.zh: 賊至無可掠，去則抄其尾。

translations.literal: When bandits came there was nothing to plunder; when they left he struck their rear.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels found nothing to loot; when they fled he struck their rear.

sentences.zh: 又擇堅寨當衝者，儲糧供給官軍。

translations.literal: He also chose strong stockades on the main routes, stored grain, and supplied government troops.
translations.idiomatic: He stocked grain in strong stockades on main routes to feed government troops.

sentences.zh: 徐天德、樊人傑敗於張家坪，因馬鞍寨阻其前，故不得竄。

translations.literal: Xu Tiande and Fan Renjie were defeated at Zhangjiaping because Ma'an Stockade blocked their front, so they could not break through.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Tiande and Fan Renjie were trapped at Zhangjiaping because Ma'an Stockade blocked their escape.

sentences.zh: 楊遇春破張天倫，亦賴太平寨夾擊之力。

translations.literal: Yang Yuchun's defeat of Zhang Tianlun also relied on Taiping Stockade's flanking strike.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuchun's defeat of Zhang Tianlun owed much to Taiping Stockade's flank attack.

sentences.zh: 以功加知州銜，賜花翎。

translations.literal: For merit he was given acting prefect rank and the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he received acting prefect rank and the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 八年，擊湖北逸匪於蜀河口，斬王祥，擒方孝德，晉秩同知直隸州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he struck Hubei fugitive bandits at Shuhekou, beheaded Wang Xiang, captured Fang Xiaode, and was advanced to subprefect of Zhili Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he struck Hubei fugitives at Shuhekou, killed Wang Xiang, captured Fang Xiaode, and rose to subprefect of Zhili Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 新設定遠廳，即以如熤補授。

translations.literal: The newly established Dingyuan Department was given to Ruyi to fill.
translations.idiomatic: The new Dingyuan Department was given to him.

sentences.zh: 九年，建新城，复於西南百餘裡黎壩、漁渡壩築二石城為犄角。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he built a new city, and again more than a hundred li to the southwest at Liba and Yuduba built two stone cities as flanking horns.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he built a new city and, a hundred li southwest, two stone forts at Liba and Yuduba as flanks.

sentences.zh: 治團如洵陽，賊至輒殲，先後擒陳心元、馮世週。

translations.literal: He governed militia as at Xunyang; when bandits came they were destroyed; he successively captured Chen Xinyuan and Feng Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled militia as at Xunyang; rebels were destroyed; he took Chen Xinyuan and Feng Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，大吏議留任，辭不可，服闋，十三年，補潼關廳。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother; great officials discussed keeping him in post but he could not be persuaded; after mourning, in the thirteenth year he was appointed to Tongguan Department.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his mother, refused to stay despite officials' pleas, and in the thirteenth year, mourning done, took Tongguan Department.

sentences.zh: 尋擢漢中知府。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted prefect of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became prefect of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 兵燹後，民困兵驕，散勇逸匪，心猶未革。

translations.literal: After the fires of war the people were distressed and the troops arrogant; disbanded braves and fugitive bandits had not yet reformed their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: After war the people were ruined, troops arrogant, disbanded braves and fugitives unreformed.

sentences.zh: 如熤聯營伍，立保甲，治堡寨，問民疾苦。

translations.literal: Ruyi linked camp units, established baojia, repaired stockades, and inquired into the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: He reorganized camps, set up baojia, repaired stockades, and asked after people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 興勸農事，行區田法，教紡織，使務本計。

translations.literal: He promoted agriculture, practiced the zone-field method, taught spinning and weaving, and made people attend to fundamental livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted farming, zone fields, spinning, and urged people back to honest livelihood.

sentences.zh: 修復褒城山河堰及城固五門、楊填二堰，各灌田數万畝，他小堰百餘，皆履勘濬治，水利普興。

translations.literal: He restored the Baocheng Shanhe Weir and the Chenggu Wumen and Yangtian weirs, each irrigating tens of thousands of mu; more than a hundred smaller weirs were all surveyed and dredged, and waterworks flourished everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: He restored Baocheng's Shanhe Weir and Chenggu's Wumen and Yangtian weirs, each watering tens of thousands of mu, dredged a hundred smaller works, and waterworks flourished.

sentences.zh: 复漢中書院，親臨講授。

translations.literal: He restored the Hanzhong Academy and lectured there in person.
translations.idiomatic: He restored Hanzhong Academy and taught there himself.

sentences.zh: 於華州渭南開諭悍回，縛獻亡命數十人；

translations.literal: At Weinan in Huazhou he admonished fierce Muslims and had dozens of fugitives bound and presented;
translations.idiomatic: At Weinan in Huazhou he persuaded fierce Muslims and sent up dozens of fugitives bound;

sentences.zh: 於寧羌解散湖北流民；

translations.literal: at Ningqiang he dispersed Hubei refugees;
translations.idiomatic: at Ningqiang he dispersed refugees from Hubei;

sentences.zh: 於城固擒教首陳恆義：皆治渠魁，寬脅從。

translations.literal: at Chenggu he captured the sect leader Chen Hengyi: in every case he punished the ringleaders and was lenient to those coerced.
translations.idiomatic: at Chenggu he seized sect leader Chen Hengyi—always punishing chiefs, sparing followers.

sentences.zh: 令行禁止，人心帖服，南山遂大定。

translations.literal: Orders were enforced and forbidden, hearts were won, and the Southern Mountains were thus greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: His orders held, hearts submitted, and the Southern Mountains were largely pacified.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，擢陝安道。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was promoted intendant of Shaan-An Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 1 he became intendant of Shaan-An Circuit.

sentences.zh: 會廷議川、楚、陝邊防建設事宜，下三省察勘，以如熤任其事，週曆相度，析官移治，增營改汛，建城口、白河、磚坪、太平、佛坪五廳，移駐文武。

translations.literal: When the court discussed frontier arrangements for Sichuan, Hubei, and Shaanxi, investigation was ordered in the three provinces; Ruyi was put in charge, traveled throughout to survey, divided offices and moved administrations, increased garrisons and changed posts, established the five departments of Chengkou, Baihe, Zhuanping, Taiping, and Foping, and moved civil and military officials to new stations.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated Sichuan-Hubei-Shaanxi frontier layout, Ruyi surveyed all three provinces, reorganized counties, added posts, founded Chengkou, Baihe, Zhuanping, Taiping, and Foping departments, and redeployed officials.

sentences.zh: 奏上，報可。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 如熤嘗言：「山內州縣距省遠，多推諉牽掣。

translations.literal: Ruyi once said: "The mountain counties are far from the provincial capital and often pass blame and hamper one another.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyi once said: "Mountain counties lie far from provincial capitals and dodge responsibility.

sentences.zh: 宜仿古梁州自為一道及明鄖陽巡撫之制，專設大員鎮撫，割三省州縣以附益之，庶勢專權一，可百世無患。」

translations.literal: One should follow the ancient Liangzhou circuit on its own and the Ming system of a Yunyang governor, appoint a high officer solely to pacify the region, and attach counties from the three provinces to strengthen it; then power would be concentrated and authority unified, and there would be no trouble for a hundred generations."
translations.idiomatic: Restore an independent Liangzhou circuit or a Yunyang governor like the Ming, attach border counties from three provinces, concentrate power, and secure the hills for generations."

sentences.zh: 以更張重大，未竟其議。

translations.literal: Because the change was too great, his proposal was not carried through.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was too sweeping and was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 三年，宣宗以如熤在陝年久，熟於南山情形，任事以來，地方安靖，特詔嘉獎，加按察使銜，以示旌異。

translations.literal: In the third year Emperor Xuanzong, because Ruyi had long been in Shaanxi and knew the Southern Mountains well and since taking office the region had been tranquil, issued a special commendation and added the rank of Provincial Surveillance Commissioner to mark exceptional honor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Xuanzong praised his long service in Shaanxi, his knowledge of the Southern Mountains, and local peace under his rule, granting the rank of Provincial Surveillance Commissioner as special honor.

sentences.zh: 巡撫盧坤尤重之，採其議增廳治於盩厔、洋縣界，增營汛於商州及略陽；

translations.literal: Governor Lu Kun especially valued him, adopted his plan to add a department seat on the border of Zhouzhi and Yang County, and increased garrison posts at Shangzhou and Lueyang;
translations.idiomatic: Governor Lu Kun especially valued him, adopted his plan to add a department seat on the border of Zhouzhi and Yang County, and increased garrison posts at Shangzhou and Lueyang;

sentences.zh: 檄勘全秦水利，於灃、涇、滻、渭諸川，鄭白、龍首諸渠，規畫俱備。

translations.literal: ordered a survey of all Qin waterworks; on the Feng, Jing, Chan, and Wei rivers and the Zheng-Bai and Longshou canals, plans were all complete.
translations.idiomatic: he ordered a survey of Qin waterways—the Feng, Jing, Chan, and Wei, the Zheng-Bai and Longshou canals—with full plans ready.

sentences.zh: 社倉、義學，亦以次推行。

translations.literal: Community granaries and charity schools were also promoted in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Community granaries and charity schools followed.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢貴州按察使，未到官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted Guizhou Provincial Surveillance Commissioner but did not reach his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was named Guizhou Provincial Surveillance Commissioner but never took office.

sentences.zh: 六年，入覲，仍調陝西，抵任數日而卒，贈布政使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he came to audience, was still transferred to Shaanxi, reached his post, and died within a few days; he was posthumously given provincial treasurer rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he had audience, returned to Shaanxi, died within days, and was posthumously made provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 陝民請比硃邑桐鄉故事，留葬南山，勿得，乃請祀名宦。

translations.literal: The people of Shaanxi asked, following the precedent of Zhu Yi in Tongxiang, to bury him in the Southern Mountains; this was not granted, and they then asked that he be entered in the temple of eminent officials.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi people asked to bury him in the Southern Mountains like Zhu Yi of Tongxiang; denied, they sought a place in the hall of worthy officials.

sentences.zh: 湖南亦祀鄉賢。

translations.literal: Hunan also entered him in the temple of local worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan honored him in the hall of local worthies as well.

sentences.zh: 如熤自為縣令至臬司，皆出特擢。

translations.literal: From magistrate to provincial judge, Ruyi's every post was a special promotion.
translations.idiomatic: From magistrate to provincial judge, every post Ruyi held was a special promotion.

sentences.zh: 在漢中十餘年不調，得成其鎮撫南山之功。

translations.literal: More than ten years at Hanzhong without transfer allowed him to complete his work of pacifying the Southern Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Ten unbroken years at Hanzhong let him finish pacifying the Southern Mountains.

sentences.zh: 宣宗每論疆吏才，必首及之。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Xuanzong discussed frontier talent, he always mentioned Ruyi first.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong, discussing frontier officials, always named Ruyi first.

sentences.zh: 將大用，已不及待。

translations.literal: He was about to be greatly employed, but could not wait.
translations.idiomatic: Greater use was coming, but death came first.

sentences.zh: 為人性豪邁，去邊幅，泊榮利，視之如田夫野老。

translations.literal: By nature he was bold and free, cast off ceremony, indifferent to glory and profit, and appeared like a farmer or rustic elder.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and plain, careless of rank and gain, he lived like a farmer.

sentences.zh: 於輿地險要，如聚米畫沙。

translations.literal: On strategic terrain he was like one piling millet to draw on sand.
translations.idiomatic: On terrain he planned as easily as piling grain to sketch on sand.

sentences.zh: 所規畫常在數十年外，措施略見所著書。

translations.literal: His designs were often decades ahead; measures are outlined in his books.
translations.idiomatic: His plans looked decades ahead; his books record his methods.

sentences.zh: 嘗佐那彥成籌海寇，有洋防備覽；

translations.literal: He once assisted Nayancheng in planning against sea pirates and wrote An Overview of Coastal Defense;
translations.idiomatic: He aided Nayancheng against pirates and wrote An Overview of Coastal Defense;

sentences.zh: 佐姜晟籌苗疆，有苗防備覽；

translations.literal: assisted Jiang Sheng in planning the Miao frontier and wrote An Overview of Miao Defense;
translations.idiomatic: aided Jiang Sheng on the Miao frontier with An Overview of Miao Defense;

sentences.zh: 佐傅鼐籌屯田，有屯防書。

translations.literal: assisted Fu Nai in planning garrison fields and wrote A Book on Garrison Defense.
translations.idiomatic: aided Fu Nai on garrison farming with A Book on Garrison Defense.

sentences.zh: 又有三省邊防備覽，漢江南北、三省山內各圖，漢中府誌及樂園詩文集。

translations.literal: He also had An Overview of the Three Provinces' Frontier Defense, maps of north and south of the Han River and of the mountain interior of the three provinces, the Hanzhong Prefecture Gazetteer, and the Leyuan collected poems and essays.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote An Overview of the Three Provinces' Frontier, maps of Han River north and south and the three provinces' hill country, the Hanzhong gazetteer, and collected poems and essays from Leyuan.

sentences.zh: 子正基，原名芝，字山舫。
