translations.literal: His son Zhengji, original name Zhi, courtesy name Shanfang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhengji, originally named Zhi, courtesy name Shanfang.

sentences.zh: 副貢生。

translations.literal: A deputy tribute graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a deputy tribute graduate.

sentences.zh: 少隨父練習吏事。

translations.literal: In youth he followed his father in practicing official business.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he learned administration at his father's side.

sentences.zh: 道光中，官河南知縣，有聲。

translations.literal: In the Daoguang period he served as magistrate in Henan and gained a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daoguang he was a Henan magistrate of note.

sentences.zh: 擢鄭州知州。

translations.literal: He was promoted department magistrate of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to department magistrate of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 治賈魯河，息水患。

translations.literal: He managed the Jialu River and ended flooding.
translations.idiomatic: He managed the Jialu River and ended its floods.

sentences.zh: 河決開封，正基佐守護。

translations.literal: When the Yellow River broke its banks at Kaifeng, Zhengji assisted in the defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River burst at Kaifeng, Zhengji helped hold the dikes.

sentences.zh: 治河兵獄，雪其冤，得河兵死力，城賴以完。

translations.literal: He cleared a case of injustice involving river soldiers, won their utmost loyalty, and the city was saved thereby.
translations.idiomatic: He righted a river-corps injustice, won their loyalty, and the city held.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸，服闋，補奉天復州。

translations.literal: He returned on mourning his mother; after mourning he was appointed to Fuzhou in Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to mourn his mother; after the mourning period he was appointed to Fuzhou in Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 興屯練，捕盜有法，民殺盜者勿論。

translations.literal: He promoted garrison militia, had effective methods for catching bandits, and people who killed bandits were not prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: He raised garrison militia, caught bandits effectively, and did not punish civilians who killed robbers.

sentences.zh: 奉天治吏素弛，府尹下所屬，以正基為法，盜風為戢。

translations.literal: Fengtian officials had long been lax; the prefect sent his subordinates to take Zhengji as their model, and banditry was curbed.
translations.idiomatic: Fengtian governance had been slack; the prefect made Zhengji the model for subordinates and banditry eased.

sentences.zh: 引疾去。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and left office.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 江南大吏疏調，擢授常州知府。

translations.literal: Great officials of Jiangnan memorialized for his transfer, and he was promoted and appointed prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan officials sought his transfer and he became prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，大水，勘災勤至，郡人感之，輸錢二十餘萬助賑，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year there was a great flood; he inspected disaster relief with tireless diligence; the people of the prefecture were moved and contributed more than two hundred thousand cash to aid relief, saving very many lives.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year great floods came; his diligent relief moved the prefecture to donate over two hundred thousand cash and save many lives.

sentences.zh: 累署淮揚道、按察使。

translations.literal: He repeatedly acted as Huai-Yang intendant and provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly acted as Huai-Yang intendant and provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，侍郎曾國籓、呂賢基交章薦之，命赴廣西治軍需，授右江道。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng, Vice Presidents Zeng Guofan and Lü Xianji jointly recommended him; he was ordered to go to Guangxi to manage military supplies and was appointed intendant of the Right River Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianfeng, Zeng Guofan and Lü Xianji recommended him; he went to Guangxi for military supplies as Right River intendant.

sentences.zh: 擢河南布政使，留廣西。

translations.literal: He was promoted Henan provincial treasurer but remained in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Henan treasurer but stayed in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 時粵匪披猖，將帥齟《齒吾》，師久無功。

translations.literal: At that time the Yue rebels were rampant; commanders were at odds and the army long achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi rebels ran wild; generals bickered and the campaign stalled.

sentences.zh: 正基曲為調和，疏論其事，謂：「師克在和，事期共濟。

translations.literal: Zhengji tactfully mediated and memorialized on the matter, saying: "An army conquers through harmony; affairs expect joint effort.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengji mediated and memorialized: "Armies win through harmony; success needs shared effort.

sentences.zh: 統兵大帥與地方大吏，宜定紛更不齊之勢，聯疏闊難合之情。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief and the local governor should fix the disorder of shifting policies and join feelings that are distant and hard to unite.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders and governors must align shifting policies and bridge distant, divided feelings.

sentences.zh: 布德信以服人心，明功罪以揚士氣。

translations.literal: Spread virtue and trust to win hearts, make merit and guilt clear to raise morale.
translations.idiomatic: Win hearts with virtue and trust; lift morale by clarifying merit and fault.

sentences.zh: 勿因賊盛而生推諉，勿因兵單而務自救，勿以小忿而不為應援，勿以偶挫而坐觀成敗。

translations.literal: Do not shirk because the rebels are strong; do not seek only your own safety because troops are few; do not withhold aid over small anger; do not sit by over a single setback and watch success or failure.
translations.idiomatic: Do not shirk because rebels are strong; do not hoard troops; do not withhold aid over petty slights; do not watch idly after one defeat.

sentences.zh: 庶逆氛可殄，大功可成。」

translations.literal: Then the rebel air can be extinguished and the great task accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: Then rebellion can be crushed and victory won."

sentences.zh: 時以為讜言。

translations.literal: At the time this was regarded as forthright counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Men called it honest counsel.

sentences.zh: 二年，桂林圍解，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the second year, when the siege of Guilin was lifted, he was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, after Guilin's siege was raised, he received the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 尋隨大軍赴湖北，時武昌初复，命馳往撫卹難民，署湖北布政使。

translations.literal: Soon he followed the main army to Hubei; Wuchang had just been recovered; he was ordered to hurry there to comfort refugees and acted as Hubei provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the main force to Hubei, comforted refugees after Wuchang's recovery, and acted as Hubei treasurer.

sentences.zh: 調廣東，复赴廣西清覈軍需。

translations.literal: Transferred to Guangdong, he again went to Guangxi to audit military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Guangdong, he again audited Guangxi military supplies.

sentences.zh: 內召授通政副使，遷通政使。

translations.literal: Summoned to the capital, he was appointed vice director of the Office of Transmission, then director.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he became vice director, then director of the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 七年，引疾歸，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he pleaded illness and returned home, then died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he resigned ill, returned home, and died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：亂之所由起與亂之所由平，亦在民之能治否耳。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Whether disorder arises and whether it is pacified also depends on whether the people can be governed.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: whether rebellion rises or falls depends on whether people can be governed.

sentences.zh: 教匪起於官逼民叛，其間獨一得民心之劉清，卒賴以招撫，助誅剿之成功。

translations.literal: The teaching rebels rose because officials drove the people to rebel; among them only Liu Qing, who won the people's hearts, finally relied on pacification to help achieve success in suppression and execution.
translations.idiomatic: Sect rebels rose from official oppression; only Liu Qing, who held the people's trust, won the war through pacification as much as the sword.

sentences.zh: 徵苗頻煩大兵，而未杜亂源，傅鼐乃以一廳一道之力，剿撫兼施，岩疆綏定。

translations.literal: Campaigns against the Miao repeatedly called out great armies yet failed to stop the source of disorder; Fu Nai with the strength of one department and one circuit, combining attack and pacification, settled the rugged frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Miao campaigns wasted great armies without ending unrest; Fu Nai, with one department and one circuit, combined war and peace and secured the rugged border.

sentences.zh: 南山善後，嚴如熤始終其事，化榛莽為桑麻。

translations.literal: The aftermath of the Southern Mountains—Yan Ruyi saw it through from start to finish, turning brambles into mulberry fields.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ruyi handled Southern Mountain recovery from first to last, turning wilderness into farmland.

sentences.zh: 此其功皆在一時節鉞之上，光於史策矣。

translations.literal: Their achievements all stood above the military banners of their day and shine in the historical record.
translations.idiomatic: Their deeds outshone the generals of their age and brighten the historical record.
